request: Edit this notice into exactly 60 words in one paragraph. Count whitespace-separated words. Preserve every practical detail.
source: The library will close on Friday at noon because the reading room ceiling needs repairs. The repair work is expected to take three days, but reopening depends on the inspection. Books due during the closure can be returned on the first day the library reopens without a late fee. Readers can use the online catalogue during the closure, although new reservations will not be processed until staff return. Please check the library website for the reopening date.
checks: Final prose has exactly 60 whitespace-separated words after all edits
One paragraph with no unrequested title or count note
Preserve closure time, reason, estimated duration, inspection condition, return policy, online access, reservation delay, and website instruction
Do not add decorative filler, duplicate an explanation, or invent a confirmed reopening date

request: Retell this short fictional scene more naturally. Keep the events and ending.
source: Mira deliberately hid the spare key. When Sol threatened to lock her in the garden, she pretended to panic. Sol locked the gate. Mira waited until he had gone, retrieved the key, and let herself out.
checks: Hiding the key stays deliberate and panic stays feigned
Preserve the sequence and the escape
Do not add reconciliation, another visit, a new helper, or a concluding moral
